paragraphs.zh: Die in den Tabellen verwendeten Abkürzungen bedeuten:
paragraphs.en: The abbreviations used in the tables have the following meanings:
paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. A small ink tick sits in the word gap between 'verwendeten' and 'Abkürzungen'; it is a scan artifact sitting above the baseline, not a character, and the two words are printed with an ordinary space between them. This line introduces the abbreviation legend that follows, which in turn serves every one of the Tabelle 1 to 5 enumeration tables that begin on this page.

paragraphs.zh: Ac = Acetyl Bu = Butyl Bz = Benzoyl Et = Ethyl Me = Methyl Pr = [illegible]Propyl c = cyclo d = Dublett m = Multiplett s = Singulett t = Triplett i = iso Fp. = Festpunkt dd = Doppelduplett
paragraphs.en: Ac = acetyl Bu = butyl Bz = benzoyl Et = ethyl Me = methyl Pr = [illegible]propyl c = cyclo d = doublet m = multiplet s = singlet t = triplet i = iso Fp. = Festpunkt (solidification point) dd = double doublet
paragraphs.notes: The abbreviation legend, laid out as three columns of 'symbol = expansion' pairs across five printed lines; transcribed here one printed line per line, reading each line left to right across all three columns. Not a prose paragraph and not a Markush enumeration table, so it is recorded as one paragraph rather than split. A dense ink blot of roughly x-height sits immediately to the left of the 'P' of 'Propyl' in the Pr entry and cannot be read: it may be an 'n' or an 'n-' prefix, giving 'n-Propyl', or it may be a scan blob, and the drawing cannot decide it, so it is recorded as [illegible] rather than guessed. Every other entry is crisp. 'Festpunkt' is printed thus and is translated literally; the abbreviation Fp. is the usual German melting-point abbreviation and elsewhere in this patent marks melting points, but the expansion the patent itself prints here is 'Festpunkt' and not 'Schmelzpunkt', so the literal reading is kept and the usual meaning is not substituted. 'Dublett', 'Doppelduplett', 'Multiplett', 'Singulett' and 'Triplett' are the German NMR multiplicity terms and are translated; 'cyclo' and 'iso' are identical in both languages.

paragraphs.zh: Tabelle 1: Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen der allgemeinen Formel (I), worin die Substituenten und Symbole folgende Bedeutungen haben: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Me R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH L = CH2 Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 2
paragraphs.en: Table 1: Compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I), in which the substituents and symbols have the following meanings: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Me R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH L = CH2 Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 2
paragraphs.notes: The Tabelle 1 caption together with the block of fixed substituent values printed directly beneath it. The caption sentence is German and is translated; the value block is chemical symbols and is identical in both fields. Superscripts are printed as superscripts on the R symbols (R with a raised 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) and as a subscript in SO2Me and CH2; they are written inline here. These values are shared by every row of the table below and by the scaffold drawn between them, and they are what the row-by-row R1 and R7 values complete. R1 and R7 are deliberately absent from this block: they are the two columns of the table.

The Tabelle 1 enumeration table as printed on this page: a shaded header row and six numbered rows. The cells are chemical symbols and NMR data, not German prose, so en repeats zh unchanged; the only German items are the column heading 'Physikalische Daten' (physical data) and the R1 value 'Benzyloxyethoxy' of Nr. 7, both left as printed so the transcription stays a faithful copy of the table. Subscripts and superscripts are written inline: the header reads R with a raised 1 and R with a raised 7, the NMR label is printed as a raised 1 before 'H NMR', and CDCl3 and the CH2, CF3, SO2 subscripts are printed as subscripts. The wide gap after each 'δ' is as printed and is preserved as a run of spaces. The table starts at Nr. 3 on this page: there is no Nr. 1 and no Nr. 2 anywhere on the page, and the header row sits directly above row 3. Row 8 is the last row on the page and its Physikalische Daten cell breaks off after '2.45 (m,2H),' at the bottom rule; it continues on the following page, and the trailing comma is as printed. The R1 cell of Nr. 5 carries a drawn ring instead of text and is recorded in drawings; the placeholder in the cell here marks its position. The R7 column is H for every row on this page. Row 6 prints its shifts out of ascending order, 7.12, 7.35, then 7.2, and row 7 lists 2.3 (s,6H) and 6.65 (s,2H) which do not obviously belong to the structure the caption defines; both are transcribed exactly as printed and are not corrected. A faint stray dot sits to the right of the '5' in the Nr. cell of row 5; it is a scan artifact, not a character.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st, the single scaffold centred between the Tabelle 1 caption block and the table header row
structures.core: two rings joined by a ketone bridge. Left ring: a saturated six-membered carbocycle drawn as a hexagon carrying one endocyclic carbon-carbon double bond, i.e. a cyclohex-2-ene-1-one bearing an enolic OH, drawn as the enol tautomer of a cyclohexane-1,3-dione. Right ring: a benzene ring drawn as a hexagon with three inner double-bond lines. The two rings are joined by a carbonyl carbon that bears a double bond to O drawn upward, a single bond down-left to the alkene carbon of the left ring and a single bond down-right to a vertex of the benzene ring
substituents: left ring, the alkene carbon bonded to the bridging carbonyl: this is the ring carbon flanked by the C=O of the ring on one side and the C-OH of the ring on the other; it carries no substituent of its own beyond the bridge
OH on the left ring at the alkene carbon at the top of that ring, the far end of the ring double bond from the bridge
=O on the left ring at the ring carbon on the other side of the bridge-bearing carbon, drawn as a ketone pointing down-right

R7 and R7 both on the same left-ring carbon, the one two bonds round from the ring ketone carbon and two bonds round from the C-OH carbon, i.e. the carbon para to the bridge-bearing carbon; one R7 is drawn out to the left on a plain bond and the second R7 is drawn downward on a plain bond, so the position is gem-disubstituted
C(=O) bridge at C1 of the benzene ring, the ring vertex on the left of that ring
Cl at C2 of the benzene ring, the vertex adjacent to C1 at the top
CH2-R1 at C3 of the benzene ring, the next vertex clockwise from Cl; the ring bond goes to a CH2 vertex which in turn carries R1 written above it
S(=O)(=O)CH3 at C4 of the benzene ring, the vertex below C3; the sulfur carries two doubly bonded O drawn below it and a CH3 drawn to the right
no substituent drawn at C5 or C6 of the benzene ring

drawings.notes: The Markush scaffold of Tabelle 1, drawn once between the caption and the table so that each row's R1 and R7 completes it. No name and no SMILES: R1 and R7 are undefined variables in the drawing, so not every atom is determined. Ring positions are read off the drawing only. The benzene numbering used above starts at the vertex bearing the bridging carbonyl and runs towards the Cl-bearing vertex; on that numbering the drawn substituent pattern is Cl, CH2R1, SO2CH3 on three consecutive vertices, which agrees with the caption's R2 = Cl, L = CH2 and R3 = SO2Me and with R4 = H, R5 = H leaving the last two vertices bare. The enolic OH on the left ring corresponds to the caption's R6 = OH. The caption also fixes Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1 and w = 2, but neither Y nor Z nor v nor w is labelled anywhere on the drawing; the left ring is simply drawn out at full size. Presented as an intermediate structure in the sense of the schema: it is a generic scaffold heading a compound table, not a step in a route, and the table is captioned 'Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen', compounds according to the invention, so it is the invention's subject matter and not prior art.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only structure inside the R1 cell of table row Nr. 5
structures.core: a saturated six-membered ring drawn as a hexagon with one ring vertex lettered O at its top-right; no inner double-bond lines, so the ring is fully saturated. This is a tetrahydropyran (oxane) ring
substituents: at the ring carbon immediately anticlockwise from the ring O, i.e. the carbon adjacent to the ring oxygen on the left-hand side: a bond going up-left to a CH2 vertex, which in turn bonds left-down to an O lettered at the far left of the cell
the left-hand lettered O is the point of attachment of the whole group to the rest of the molecule; its bond to the parent is not drawn, the cell simply ends there
no other substituent is drawn anywhere on the ring
structures.name: (oxan-2-yl)methoxy, i.e. (tetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-yl)methoxy

drawings.notes: This is the R1 value of table row Nr. 5 of Tabelle 1, drawn as a small structure in the cell instead of written as text; it is the only cell on the page that does so. Read atom by atom off the drawing: attachment O, then CH2, then a ring carbon that sits next to the ring oxygen, then four further CH2 round to that oxygen, six ring atoms in all with exactly one of them O. The SMILES uses * for the open attachment point at the left-hand O and encodes nothing that is not drawn; the ring carbon bearing the CH2 is a stereocentre but no wedge, hash or stereo label is drawn, so no configuration is recorded. The row's own NMR data, 1.55 (m,6H), 3.6 (m,2H), 3.95 (m,2H), 4.3 (m,1H), is consistent with a 2-substituted tetrahydropyran but was not used to read the drawing.

discrepancies.what: The scaffold draws two separate substituents on one ring carbon and labels both R7, while the table offers only a single R7 column with one value per row.
discrepancies.drawing_says: two plain bonds from the same left-ring carbon, one going left and one going down, each labelled R7
discrepancies.text_says: a single column headed R7, giving H for each of rows 3 to 8

discrepancies.what: The caption fixes Y, Z, v and w, but none of those four symbols appears anywhere on the drawn scaffold.
discrepancies.drawing_says: the left ring is drawn out explicitly as a six-membered carbocycle with no Y, Z, v or w labels on it
discrepancies.text_says: Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1, w = 2

illegible: A dense ink blot roughly the height of a lowercase letter sits immediately to the left of the 'P' of 'Propyl' in the 'Pr =' entry of the abbreviation legend, third column of the second legend line. It may be an 'n' or an 'n-' prefix, or it may be a scan blob; it cannot be resolved at the available resolution.
